questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best places in the world to go whale watching
How whales communicate with songs
How humans' relationship with whales has changed over time
Why whales swim so fast
questions.why: Phil says they'll discuss our past and present relationship with these giants of the ocean.

questions.q: What wild animals have Georgie and Phil seen?
options: Georgie saw a baby badger; Phil saw whales
They both saw whales on holiday together
Phil saw a badger, and Georgie saw a whale
Neither of them has seen a wild animal
questions.why: Georgie saw a baby badger on a walk; Phil saw whales from the coast in Patagonia.

questions.q: What does Phil say about the International Whaling Commission's ban?
options: It ended last year after many arguments
It was ignored by almost every country
It only protects blue whales, not others
It saved many species, but some still hunt
questions.why: He says Japan, Iceland and Norway still hunt, but the ban has saved many species from extinction.

questions.q: Why was early whaling often unsuccessful?
options: Slow wooden boats couldn't catch fast whales
There were very few whales in the oceans
Whaling was illegal in most countries
Hunters didn't know where whales lived
questions.why: Hunters used slow-moving wooden boats, and big whales can swim up to 30km/hr.

questions.q: What changed whaling in the late 1800s, according to Jayne Pierce?
options: A new law in Norway
The invention of the exploding harpoon
The discovery of new whale species
Better maps of the ocean
questions.why: She says Svend Foyn invented the exploding harpoon, a turning point for the whale.

questions.q: Why does Georgie say the harpoon was a turning point 'sadly not in this case'?
options: Because the new invention didn't really work
Because it made whales much harder to find
Because the change was bad for whales
Because Svend Foyn was not a real whaler
questions.why: A turning point usually means change for the better, but it led to far more whales being killed.

questions.q: How many whales had been killed by the time many species faced extinction?
options: About 30,000
About 300,000
Exactly one million
Over three million
questions.why: Phil says over three million whales had been killed and many species faced extinction.

questions.q: Why does marine biologist Joe Roman praise Greenpeace?
options: They made the first recordings of whale song
They blocked hunters with boats and used media
They paid several countries to stop whaling
They invented a new way to count whales
questions.why: He says they put their boats between Soviet hunting vessels and whales, and were 'very good at media'.
